# Assumption of Moses Chapter 1 — The PNEUMA Bible (Dynamic)
**Translator:** PNEUMA | **Source:** Latin palimpsest (Codex Ambrosianus) | **Section:** Moses' Farewell Commission to Joshua

---

**1** This is the testament of Moses. He delivered it in the one hundred and twentieth year of his life — the two thousand five hundredth year since the creation of the world, and the one hundred and twentieth year after the departure from Phoenicia, when the people came out after the exodus Moses led from Egypt.

**2** According to the reckoning of years written in the covenant, after Moses had received his prophetic commission from God, and after the departure of the children of Israel — Moses speaking from a book in the fortieth year in the wilderness.

**3** Moses called Joshua son of Nun to him and said:

**4** Pay close attention to everything I am about to tell you, Joshua son of Nun. God chose me to serve his people — to make the covenant with them and to be the mediator of that covenant.

**5** From the beginning of creation to the end of time, Moses was prepared to be the mediator of God's covenant.

**6** And the Lord said to me: I appointed you from the very beginning of the world to be the mediator of the covenant.

**7** Receive these writings so that you will know how to preserve the books I am entrusting to you.

**8** Arrange them, anoint them with cedar oil, and store them in clay vessels in the place that God prepared from the very beginning of creation.

**9** For these shall be the testimony of God.

**10** God has appointed me to pray for the sins of his people and to intercede for them.

**11** It is not because of any virtue of mine or any physical strength I have, but because of his compassion and his long-suffering that he has endured with them and nourished them.

**12** For thus says the Lord of the world: he created the world for the sake of his people, but he did not reveal this purpose from the beginning,

**13** so that the nations would be judged for their wickedness, and would be humiliated through the very nations he himself had made, so that his purpose would be made manifest.

**14** Yes, he devised and planned everything on their behalf, and he prepared and appointed me from the beginning of the world to be the mediator of his covenant.

**15** And now I am about to go to sleep with my fathers, and you will lead the people into the land he has prepared for them.
